title: Work as Flow
coreMove: Redesign a work task so it answers back with challenge and feedback instead of waiting for leisure to supply all meaning.
sourcePressure: Work can become a primary flow site when autonomy, challenge, skill, goals, and feedback line up, even though people often expect leisure to provide the better life.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Romanticize all jobs or tell exploited workers to enjoy bad conditions.

sourceAnchors.name: the paradox of work
sourceAnchors.detail: the frozen contents list the paradox of work as a Chapter 7 subheading
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The paradox of work is that people often report richer structure there, then spend the day dreaming of free time they may not know how to use.

sourceAnchors.name: autotelic jobs
sourceAnchors.detail: the frozen contents list autotelic jobs as a Chapter 7 subheading
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: An autotelic job is not a dream title; it is work arranged so the doing itself can become absorbing.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm - a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

exampleSpecs.domain: a municipal permit clerk changing how applications answer back
exampleSpecs.audience: office workers in repetitive public-service roles
exampleSpecs.stakes: mistakes delay housing permits and make the day feel pointless
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he chooses whether to batch-stamp forms mechanically or create a visible error pattern board that turns the queue into a solvable process
exampleSpecs.firstImage: At 9:03 a.m., David lifts the first permit folder

exampleSpecs.domain: a hotel laundry supervisor finding feedback in turnaround flow
exampleSpecs.audience: service managers whose work is invisible when it goes right
exampleSpecs.stakes: late linens ripple into guest complaints before dinner
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she traces yesterday's late carts to one hidden bottleneck and marks a new load sequence by floor
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Warm cotton fogs the laundry room windows

exampleSpecs.domain: an apprentice electrician choosing a harder wiring run
exampleSpecs.audience: tradespeople balancing speed and skill growth
exampleSpecs.stakes: choosing only easy jobs keeps him fast but stagnant
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: his foreman asks which run will teach him, and Jack takes the conduit bend that gives immediate visible feedback
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Which one will teach you something?" the foreman asks

exampleSpecs.domain: a call-center lead redesigning free time after a structured shift
exampleSpecs.audience: workers who feel engaged at work and empty after clock-out
exampleSpecs.stakes: her evening can collapse into passive exhaustion despite a competent day
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: ask why the shift felt more alive than the evening, then show her adding one goal and feedback loop to a language practice block
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Why did the shift feel clearer than the free evening?

exampleSpecs.domain: a freelance illustrator replacing vague client work with milestones
exampleSpecs.stakes: the contract deadline is close and no manager will define progress
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the studio wall has blank space, and Ryan turns the commission into six visible thumbnails with one client feedback gate
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The north wall of the studio is still bare

exampleSpecs.domain: a lab sterilization tech protecting dignity in constrained work
exampleSpecs.audience: workers in necessary jobs with limited autonomy
exampleSpecs.stakes: the job cannot be made glamorous, but one controllable skill loop can reduce drift and errors
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: you cannot rename the job, but you can decide whether each tray returns as a blur or as a timed accuracy challenge with a clean handoff
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You slide the twelfth instrument tray under the lamp

skillTargets: adding agency without denying bad conditions
turning routine work into structured challenge where possible

tryThisNowSpec: Pick one work task you resent, name the feedback it currently hides, and add one visible checkpoint before the next attempt.
